preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is an integer between 1 and 5 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(Q, int) and 1 <= Q <= 100000 for Q in test_cases_Q)
preconditions.description: For each test case, the number of queries Q is an integer between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(all(isinstance(X, int) and 1 <= X <= 100000 for X in queries) for queries in all_test_case_queries)
preconditions.description: For each query in every test case, the integer X is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

postconditions.expression: len(stdout_lines) == sum(len(queries) for queries in all_test_case_queries)
postconditions.description: The total number of output lines equals the total number of queries across all test cases.

postconditions.expression: all(' ' in line and len(line.split()) == 2 for line in stdout_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output line contains exactly two space-separated integers.

postconditions.expression: all(E >= 0 and O >= 0 for E, O in parsed_output)
postconditions.description: The counts E (even parity) and O (odd parity) are non-negative integers.

postconditions.expression: all(E + O == len(S_final) for (E, O), S_final in zip(parsed_output, final_sets))
postconditions.description: For each query, the sum of E and O equals the total number of elements in the set S after the update.

postconditions.expression: all(E == sum(1 for x in S if bin(x).count('1') % 2 == 0) and O == sum(1 for x in S if bin(x).count('1') % 2 == 1) for (E, O), S in zip(parsed_output, final_sets))
postconditions.description: E is the count of elements in S with an even number of 1s in binary, and O is the count of elements with an odd number of 1s.

postconditions.expression: all(S_next == S_prev | {X} | {y ^ X for y in S_prev if y != X} for S_prev, S_next, X in zip(initial_and_intermediate_sets, final_sets, all_queries))
postconditions.description: The set S after each query is the union of the previous set, the new element X, and all XOR combinations of X with existing elements (excluding X itself if it was already present, though set logic handles duplicates).
